title: From passage to practice.
subtitle: Factual question generation with source evidence and independent answerability checks.
notes: Introduce the task: educational text plus an intended answer becomes a factual question. We compare a cheap baseline, pretrained sequence-to-sequence models and an English LoRA extension. The final rubric requires code, 8–12 slides and a demo, not a standalone report. Substantial Codex assistance is disclosed in AI_ASSISTANCE.md; the student should understand and review the implementation.

title: Ask about a fact. Keep the evidence.
subtitle: A question should be relevant, answerable from the passage, and useful to a learner.
notes: The main experiment is answer-conditioned QG. Both baseline and Transformer see context and target answer. TF-IDF answer selection is a separate application feature, not part of the controlled benchmark score. Independent QA asks the generated question and compares its extracted answer with the target. It is a proxy rather than a guarantee of factuality.

title: Three languages. Documented data.
subtitle: Human-annotated public benchmarks plus a small original parallel classroom supplement.
notes: Public sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/rajpurkar/squad (CC-BY-SA-4.0), https://huggingface.co/datasets/lincoln/newsquadfr (CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0), https://huggingface.co/datasets/hsseinmz/arcd (MIT in Hub metadata; Wikipedia attribution also applies). Actual counts and exclusions are in results/data/manifest.json. Different domains prevent a controlled ranking of languages. Original scenarios are AI-assisted and need human review; translations of one topic stay in one split.

title: Preserve language. Prevent paragraph leakage.
subtitle: Natural text and exact offsets enter the pretrained tokenizer unchanged.
notes: Validate answer text at its original character offset; do not guess repairs. Exclude duplicate question/answer records. Reserve evaluation paragraphs and remove matches from training. Split remaining training paragraphs into train/development, then sample one question per paragraph with seed 42. Accents/Arabic are preserved. Grouping is exact normalized paragraph grouping, not near-duplicate or article isolation. EDA records length distributions. Cropping measures the actual prompt and retains the answer; surrounding context can be lost.

title: A cheap baseline. A learned rewrite.
subtitle: Identical context and target answers make the comparison interpretable.
notes:
Baseline: source sentence with the exact target replaced by a language-specific WH phrase. This retains source content but often yields unnatural grammar. Neural models learn conditional rewriting and question syntax. English: lmqg/t5-small-squad-qg; French: lmqg/mt5-small-frquad-qg; Arabic: Mihakram/AraT5-base-question-generation. Input formats and pinned revisions are documented in registry.py and DATA_AND_MODELS.md. Different language checkpoints are not matched in parameter count or training data.

Illustrative source example selected for readability, not to estimate average quality. Record ID: en:57114667a58dae1900cd6d80.

title: Attention generates. LoRA adapts.
subtitle: Encoder–decoder generation with a bounded English training experiment.
notes:
The encoder uses bidirectional self-attention. The decoder uses causal self-attention and cross-attention to encoder states, generating one token at a time. Unlike decoder-only GPT-2, it explicitly conditions on encoded input. LoRA learns low-rank BA updates to frozen query/value projections: W_eff = W + (alpha/r)BA. The rank-8 adapter uses alpha 16 and dropout 0.05. Development token cross-entropy selects the checkpoint, including the initial step. Test data never enters training or selection. Source papers: https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10683 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11934 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12068 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17416 .

LoRA method reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685 . Training-loss figure is included in results/data/lora_loss_curve.png. The loss reduction is small and is not a quality guarantee.

title: Fixed settings. Paired comparisons.
subtitle: Do not choose hyperparameters using the final test results.
notes: Configuration is recorded in results/*/config.json along with input hashes and checkpoint commits; environment.json records versions and git commit. Cold model loading is excluded from per-example generation latency and reported separately. All methods evaluate identical IDs. Errors remain in denominators. LoRA trains at 256 input tokens for cost control, then evaluates at the common 384-token budget. This tests a small practical adaptation, not a full training sweep. Single-reference overlap is imperfect. Paragraph-group bootstrap intervals estimate sampling variability, not systematic error.

title: Measured benchmark results
subtitle: Question agreement and round-trip QA are complementary, imperfect signals.
notes: Read the figure from actual result files. chrF++ and ROUGE-L are reference agreement, not factual correctness. QA token F1 compares the independent answer with the intended target. Error bars resample paragraph groups. Avoid claiming a clear improvement when paired confidence intervals cross zero. Language differences combine domain, checkpoint size/training and verifier quality. See summary.csv, predictions.jsonl and paired_comparisons.json for complete numbers and failures.

title: Check the questions—and the judge.
subtitle: The verifier is multilingual-pretrained, but QA-fine-tuned on English SQuAD2.
notes:
Verifier source: https://huggingface.co/deepset/xlm-roberta-base-squad2-distilled . Reference questions are positive controls; unrelated questions ask for a red submarine's serial number. High reference F1 supports usefulness of the verifier on that language/domain; low reference F1 makes generated-question failures ambiguous. Nonzero unrelated target agreement exposes false positives. The rule requires F1>=0.5, nonempty span score>=0.1 and no answer leakage. Coverage is not human accuracy. QA span scores are uncalibrated, and lexical cosine is not semantic entailment.

This probe was added after observing a perfect-QA but unfaithful David/Trajan's Column question. It is exploratory and does not tune generation or review thresholds. Unsupported Mars qualifiers pass the fixed rules in 1/24 EN, 10/24 FR, 12/24 AR cases. The labels indicate unsupported premises in these constructed questions, not real-world truth or general false-positive rates. Main beam-4 coverage: EN 90.0%, FR 62.5%, AR 40.0%; coverage is not accuracy.

title: Failures are part of the result.
subtitle: Source-inspected examples distinguish generation mistakes from judge mistakes.
notes:
These illustrative cases were selected purposively with disclosed AI-assisted qualitative inspection. They are not blinded human ratings or error-prevalence estimates. Inspect the source evidence and the intended relation. human_review.csv remains blank for student/human annotation. Additional cases and full source passages are in results/qualitative_examples.json.

EN en:572a07c11d046914007796d8: The intended answer explains why the tribe maps its lands: strengthening territorial claims. The generated 'How' question asks for the mechanism, GPS/Google Earth. The question is answerable, but asks about a different fact than its supplied target.
Source: Using handheld GPS devices and programs like Google Earth, members of the Trio Tribe, who live in the rainforests of southern Suriname, map out their ancestral lands to help strengthen their territorial claims.

FR fr:2739: The target is Ankara, which provided military assistance. The generated question asks who was attacked and the verifier extracts pro-Haftar. Asking about an affected party changes the relation from the source reference's assisting party.
Source: Aidés militairement par Ankara, les pro-GNA ont engrangé d'importantes victoires ces derniers mois prenant le contrôle de l'ensemble du nord-ouest et chassant les pro-Haftar qui menaient depuis avril 2019 une offensive pour prendre la capitale Tripoli.

AR ar:550131195698: The generated Arabic question is exactly the reference: 'Who is Jundah's father?' The passage begins Jundah ibn Hujr ibn al-Harith. Both verifier runs select Kinda, the tribe, rather than Hujr. Here low QA F1 is a verifier error, not evidence that question generation failed.
Source: جندح بن حُجر بن الحارث الكندي (500 - 540 م) اشتُهر بلقب اُمْرُؤ القَيْس، هو شاعرعربي من مكانة رفيعة، بَرز في فترةِ الجاهلية، ويُعد رأس شعراء العرب، وأحد أبرزهم في التاريخ، اختلفت المصادر في تسميته، فورد باسم جندح وحندج ومليكة وعدي، وهو من قبيلة كندة.

title: Ready to demonstrate. Clear about the limits.
subtitle: A working learning tool, with an auditable experiment behind it.
notes:
Demonstrate English, French and Arabic; show evidence and review reasons; export student worksheet and answer key. Original parallel scenarios supplement the public benchmark but are small and AI-assisted. Upstream exposure, limited human annotation, single references and cross-lingual verifier weakness limit conclusions. Next: human ratings from two reviewers, near-duplicate/article isolation, stronger multilingual verification and independently authored educational data. AI assistance is disclosed. Personalize and rehearse the slides before submission.
